text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.7% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 8.8%. The drop reflects a broad unwinding of the refinery boom that had driven these stocks higher — a November 23rd report explicitly noted "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," signaling that traders are rotating out of the sector after an extended run. Oil prices remain firm (U.S. crude at $89.53/barrel), and refineries are running at 95.7% capacity, so the fundamental backdrop hasn't collapsed; rather, sentiment has shifted as the profit tailwinds that fueled the rally are fading.

The timing coincides with softening geopolitical risk premiums around Middle East tensions. While Iranian sanctions escalated and Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities continued through the week, oil markets absorbed the news without sharp spikes—suggesting traders no longer see these conflicts as near-term supply threats. Combined with climate talks collapsing (which removes near-term policy headwinds for fossil fuels but also signals a reversal of regulatory tailwinds), the stock is caught in a rotation out of energy into other sectors.
